grok.rationale: At closing, FGL's annuity and life product lines crossed with FGL surviving as the operating subsidiary, and the Merger Agreement required ordinary-course conduct and preservation of the business organization, so customer-facing products and the processes that produce them moved together (gap_45=0). Continuing FGL operating management (Littlefield, Marhoun, Vigneau and certain other current managers) and twelve-month employee compensation/benefits protections were locked in alongside those operations, while the new Blackstone Investment Management Agreement expressly aligned the re-engineered general-account investment process with a designated manager rather than leaving processes without an organization (gap_56=0).

openai.rationale: The customer-facing annuity and life-insurance product lines crossed with surviving FGL, but a core supporting process—general-account investment management—did not transfer unchanged and was instead assigned under a new Investment Management Agreement to a newly formed Blackstone subsidiary, documenting a T4–T5 mismatch at closing. That re-engineered process was operated by a separate Blackstone organization rather than the transferring FGL organization, documenting a T5–T6 boundary mismatch. The Investment Management Agreement contractually bridged both mismatches, while the employee-matters provisions separately preserved continuity for FGL personnel.
